sum: A loop from Jomsom up the Kali Gandaki to Lo Manthang and back by Lo Gekar and Dhakmar, crossing a string of passes around 4,000 m in dry, wind-scoured country behind the Himalaya.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Upper Mustang is a restricted area. The permit is issued only through a registered agency and you must walk with a licensed guide; the checkpoint at Kagbeni records every group. Since 22 March 2026 the Department of Immigration issues the permit to a single trekker as well, so you no longer need a partner to apply. A local guide also finds the foot trails that avoid the road and the key-holders for locked temples and caves.

access: Fly from Pokhara to Jomsom in about 20 minutes, or take a jeep or bus up the Kali Gandaki road via Beni and Tatopani. Flights leave early and are cancelled when wind or cloud builds, so keep a spare day or be ready to switch to the road.

photo.a: Weathered chortens painted white, grey, red and yellow stand on a stony plain in front of the fluted red and ochre cliffs of Dhakmar.
photo.c: Chortens below the red cliffs of Dhakmar

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
ACAP permit; the restricted-area permit in most packages (confirm)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
transport between Pokhara and Jomsom (flight or jeep; confirm which)

permits.name: Upper Mustang restricted area permit
permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu (the Pokhara immigration office also issues them), through a registered trekking agency only.

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, and a flight or a jeep seat between Pokhara and Jomsom each way
tips: The restricted-area permit is charged at USD 50 per person per day; the older flat ten-day fee no longer applies. Count the days with your agency before they apply: the clock runs from the Kagbeni checkpoint until you pass it again, ten days on this plan.
Bring all your cash from Pokhara or Jomsom. There are no dependable cash machines north of Jomsom.
Start walking by 7 am and aim to arrive by early afternoon, before the wind is at its worst.
Temples in Lo Manthang, Tsarang and Lo Gekar charge entry fees and do not allow photographs inside; carry small notes.
Pass names and heights differ between maps, and the points where the foot trail leaves the road change as the road is rebuilt, so treat the heights and walking times here as approximate.

days.t: Fly to Jomsom, walk to Kagbeni
days.note: After the morning flight, follow the wide gravel bed of the Kali Gandaki or the jeep road on its east bank. The wind gets up from the south by late morning and is at your back; cover your nose and mouth when vehicles pass. Your permits are registered at Kagbeni.
why: A jump from 822 m to sleep at 2,810 m in a single day.

n: Show Boat Hotel - Ama chorten cafe

days.note: North of the checkpoint you are in the restricted area. Most of the day is on or beside the road along the east bank, with short trail sections through Tangbe and Chhusang. Cross the bridge where the river runs under a block of red rock and finish with a steep half-hour climb to Chele.

A big day uphill. The trail climbs a canyon wall to the Taklam La and Dajori La, drops to the poplars of Samar for lunch, then crosses two more ridges, the Bhena La and Yamda La. If you have the energy, the lower foot trail by Chungsi cave avoids the road but adds about an hour.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 750 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.t: Syangboche to Ghami over the Nyi La
days.note: A short climb over the Syangboche La, then a long gentle descent into the valley of Ghiling. From there the trail climbs steadily to the Nyi La, the highest point of the walk in, and drops to Ghami across the smaller Ghami La. Expect strong wind on the passes from midday.

Drop to the river below Ghami and pass the longest mani wall in Mustang, built of stone painted ochre, white and grey. A steady climb leads to the Tsarang La and a long, easy descent to Tsarang. Leave time in the afternoon for the dzong and the monastery.

Cross the Tsarang Khola canyon and climb gradually north past a large solitary chorten. Foot trail and road run close together for much of the morning. From the Lo La the walled town appears below, and you reach the gate about half an hour later.

days.t: Lo Manthang and the Chhoser caves
days.note: Visit the Jampa, Thubchen and Chode temples inside the walls in the morning. In the afternoon most people go by jeep or horse to Chhoser for the Jhong cave and Nyphu monastery; on foot it is about two hours each way along a gently rising valley.

days.t: Lo Manthang to Dhakmar via Lo Gekar
days.note: The longest and highest day, and the best one for getting off the road. A dry three-hour climb leads to the Chogo La, then the trail drops to Lo Gekar monastery, crosses the Mui La and descends a steep gully through red cliffs to Dhakmar. Carry lunch and at least two litres of water.

An easy hour down the valley to Ghami, where you rejoin the outward route. Climb back over the Ghami La and Nyi La before the wind gets up, then leave the main trail and drop into Ghiling, which most groups only see from above on the way north.

Retrace the ridge route over the Syangboche La and Yamda La to Samar, then lose height quickly down the canyon to Chele and the river. Mostly downhill but long, and the last stretch along the valley floor is into the wind.

A long road day back down the Kali Gandaki, checking out of the restricted area at Kagbeni. The wind is in your face from late morning, so start at first light. Many groups take a jeep for part or all of this stage, and you miss little by doing so.
Morning flight to Pokhara, weather permitting. If flights are cancelled, jeeps and buses leave Jomsom for Pokhara through the morning and take most of the day.
